whatItIs.text: The fresh leaves of the coriander plant (the seeds are the spice called coriander); to most people they taste fresh and citrusy, though a gene variant makes some find them soapy.

historyNote.text: Coriander is native to the Mediterranean Basin, and its old Greek name came from koris, a bed bug, because of the plant's pungency before flowering.

howToChoose.text: Choose bunches with perky, deep green leaves and no slimy or yellowing patches; roots intact if you can get them.

storage.text: Stand in a jar of water like flowers, loosely bagged in the fridge, or wrap in slightly damp paper.

useItUp.text: Wilted coriander still works chopped into chutneys, blended into dressing, or frozen in ice-cube trays with water or oil.

substitutions.note: similar freshness without the citrus-soapy note; safe for coriander haters
